verses.en: Then Agrippa said unto Paul, Thou art permitted to speak for thyself. Then Paul stretched forth the hand, and answered for himself:
verses.pt: E Agripa disse a Paulo: É permitido a ti falar por ti mesmo.Então Paulo, estendendo a mão, respondeu em sua defesa:
verses.en_web: Agrippa said to Paul, “You may speak for yourself.” Then Paul stretched out his hand, and made his defense.
verses.en_bbe: And Agrippa said to Paul, You may put your cause before us. Then Paul, stretching out his hand, made his answer, saying:

verses.en: I think myself happy, king Agrippa, because I shall answer for myself this day before thee touching all the things whereof I am accused of the Jews:
verses.pt: Eu me considero feliz, rei Agripa, de que diante de ti eu esteja hoje fazendo minha defesa de todas as coisas de que sou acusado pelos judeus;
verses.en_web: “I think myself happy, King Agrippa, that I am to make my defense before you today concerning all the things that I am accused by the Jews,
verses.en_bbe: In my opinion I am happy, King Agrippa, to be able to give my answer before you today to all these things which the Jews say against me:

verses.en: Especially because I know thee to be expert in all customs and questions which are among the Jews: wherefore I beseech thee to hear me patiently.
verses.pt: Principalmente por eu saber que tu sabes de todos os costumes e questões que há entre os judeus; por isso eu te rogo que tu me ouças com paciência.
verses.en_web: especially because you are expert in all customs and questions which are among the Jews. Therefore I beg you to hear me patiently.
verses.en_bbe: The more so, because you are expert in all questions to do with the Jews and their ways: so I make my request to you to give me a hearing to the end.

verses.en: My manner of life from my youth, which was at the first among mine own nation at Jerusalem, know all the Jews;
verses.pt: Ora, a minha vida é conhecida por todos os judeus, desde a minha juventude, que desde o princípio tem sido entre os de minha nação em Jerusalém;
verses.en_web: “Indeed, all the Jews know my way of life from my youth up, which was from the beginning among my own nation and at Jerusalem;
verses.en_bbe: All the Jews have knowledge of my way of life from my early years, as it was from the start among my nation, and at Jerusalem;

verses.en: Which knew me from the beginning, if they would testify, that after the most straitest sect of our religion I lived a Pharisee.
verses.pt: Eles me conhecem desde o começo, se quiserem testemunhar, de que conforme a mais rigorosa divisão de nossa religião, eu vivi como fariseu.
verses.en_web: having known me from the first, if they are willing to testify, that after the strictest sect of our religion I lived a Pharisee.
verses.en_bbe: And they are able to say, if they would give witness, that I was living as a Pharisee, in that division of our religion which is most regular in the keeping of the law.

verses.en: And now I stand and am judged for the hope of the promise made of God unto our fathers:
verses.pt: E agora, pela esperança da promessa que por Deus foi dada aos nossos pais, eu estou aqui sendo julgado.
verses.en_web: Now I stand here to be judged for the hope of the promise made by God to our fathers,
verses.en_bbe: And now I am here to be judged because of the hope given by God's word to our fathers;

verses.en: Unto which promise our twelve tribes, instantly serving God day and night, hope to come. For which hope’s sake, king Agrippa, I am accused of the Jews.
verses.pt: À qual nossas doze tribos, servindo continuamente a Deus de dia e de noite, esperam chegar; pela qual esperança, rei Agripa, eu sou acusado pelos judeus.
verses.en_web: which our twelve tribes, earnestly serving night and day, hope to attain. Concerning this hope I am accused by the Jews, King Agrippa!
verses.en_bbe: For the effecting of which our twelve tribes have been working and waiting night and day with all their hearts. And in connection with this hope I am attacked by the Jews, O king!

verses.en: Why should it be thought a thing incredible with you, that God should raise the dead?
verses.pt: Por que se julga como incrível entre vós que Deus ressuscite aos mortos?
verses.en_web: Why is it judged incredible with you, if God does raise the dead?
verses.en_bbe: Why, in your opinion, is it outside belief for God to make the dead come to life again?

verses.en: I verily thought with myself, that I ought to do many things contrary to the name of Jesus of Nazareth.
verses.pt: Eu realmente tinha pensado comigo mesmo, que contra o nome de Jesus eu tinha que fazer muitas oposições.
verses.en_web: “I myself most certainly thought that I ought to do many things contrary to the name of Jesus of Nazareth.
verses.en_bbe: For I, truly, was of the opinion that it was right for me to do a number of things against the name of Jesus of Nazareth.

verses.en: Which thing I also did in Jerusalem: and many of the saints did I shut up in prison, having received authority from the chief priests; and when they were put to death, I gave my voice against them.
verses.pt: O que eu também fiz em Jerusalém; e tendo recebido autoridade dos chefes dos sacerdotes, eu pus em prisões a muitos dos santos; e quando eles eram mortos, eu também dava meu voto contra eles.
verses.en_web: This I also did in Jerusalem. I both shut up many of the saints in prisons, having received authority from the chief priests, and when they were put to death I gave my vote against them.
verses.en_bbe: And this I did in Jerusalem: and numbers of the saints I put in prison, having had authority given to me from the chief priests, and when they were put to death, I gave my decision against them.

verses.en: And I punished them oft in every synagogue, and compelled them to blaspheme; and being exceedingly mad against them, I persecuted them even unto strange cities.
verses.pt: E tendo lhes dado punição muitas vezes por todas as sinagogas, eu os forcei a blasfemarem. E estando extremamente enfurecido contra eles, até nas cidades estrangeiras eu os persegui;
verses.en_web: Punishing them often in all the synagogues, I tried to make them blaspheme. Being exceedingly enraged against them, I persecuted them even to foreign cities.
verses.en_bbe: And I gave them punishment frequently, in all the Synagogues, forcing them to say things against God; and burning with passion against them, I went after them even into far-away towns.

verses.en: Whereupon as I went to Damascus with authority and commission from the chief priests,
verses.pt: Nas quais, indo eu até Damasco, com autoridade e comissão dos chefes dos sacerdotes;
verses.en_web: “Whereupon as I traveled to Damascus with the authority and commission from the chief priests,
verses.en_bbe: Then, when I was journeying to Damascus with the authority and orders of the chief priests,

verses.en: At midday, O king, I saw in the way a light from heaven, above the brightness of the sun, shining round about me and them which journeyed with me.
verses.pt: Ao meio dia, vi no caminho, rei, uma luz do céu, que brilhava muito mais que o sol, e que encheu de claridade ao redor de mim e dos que iam comigo.
verses.en_web: at noon, O king, I saw on the way a light from the sky, brighter than the sun, shining around me and those who traveled with me.
verses.en_bbe: In the middle of the day, on the road I saw a light from heaven, brighter than the sun, shining round me and those who were journeying with me.

verses.en: And when we were all fallen to the earth, I heard a voice speaking unto me, and saying in the Hebrew tongue, Saul, Saul, why persecutest thou me? it is hard for thee to kick against the pricks.
verses.pt: E todos nós, tendo caído ao chão, eu ouvi uma voz que falava a mim, e dizia em língua hebraica: Saulo, Saulo, por que me persegues? Duro é para ti dar coices contra os aguilhões.
verses.en_web: When we had all fallen to the earth, I heard a voice saying to me in the Hebrew language, ‘Saul, Saul, why are you persecuting me? It is hard for you to kick against the goads.’
verses.en_bbe: And when we had all gone down on the earth, a voice came to me, saying in the Hebrew language, Saul, Saul, why are you attacking me so cruelly? It is hard for you to go against the impulse which is driving you.

verses.en: And I said, Who art thou, Lord? And he said, I am Jesus whom thou persecutest.
verses.pt: E eu disse: Quem és, Senhor? E ele disse: Eu sou Jesus, a quem tu persegues.
verses.en_web: “I said, ‘Who are you, Lord?’ “He said, ‘I am Jesus, whom you are persecuting.
verses.en_bbe: And I said, Who are you, Lord? And the Lord said, I am Jesus, whom you are attacking.

verses.en: But rise, and stand upon thy feet: for I have appeared unto thee for this purpose, to make thee a minister and a witness both of these things which thou hast seen, and of those things in the which I will appear unto thee;
verses.pt: Mas levanta-te, e fica de pé, porque para isto eu apareci a ti, para te predeterminar como trabalhador e testemunha, tanto das coisas que já tens visto, como das coisas que eu ainda aparecerei a ti;
verses.en_web: But arise, and stand on your feet, for I have appeared to you for this purpose: to appoint you a servant and a witness both of the things which you have seen, and of the things which I will reveal to you;
verses.en_bbe: But get up on your feet: for I have come to you for this purpose, to make you a servant and a witness of the things in which you have seen me, and of those in which you will see me;

verses.en: Delivering thee from the people, and from the Gentiles, unto whom now I send thee,
verses.pt: Livrando-te d este povo, e dos gentios, aos quais agora eu te envio.
verses.en_web: delivering you from the people, and from the Gentiles, to whom I send you,
verses.en_bbe: And I will keep you safe from the people, and from the Gentiles, to whom I send you,

verses.en: To open their eyes, and to turn them from darkness to light, and from the power of Satan unto God, that they may receive forgiveness of sins, and inheritance among them which are sanctified by faith that is in me.
verses.pt: Para abrir os olhos deles, e das trevas converterem à luz, e do poder de Satanás converterem a Deus; para que recebam perdão dos pecados, e herança entre os santificados pela fé em mim.
verses.en_web: to open their eyes, that they may turn from darkness to light and from the power of Satan to God, that they may receive remission of sins and an inheritance among those who are sanctified by faith in me.’
verses.en_bbe: To make their eyes open, turning them from the dark to the light, and from the power of Satan to God, so that they may have forgiveness of sins and a heritage among those who are made holy by faith in me.

verses.en: Whereupon, O king Agrippa, I was not disobedient unto the heavenly vision:
verses.pt: Portanto, rei Agripa, eu não fui desobediente à visão celestial.
verses.en_web: “Therefore, King Agrippa, I was not disobedient to the heavenly vision,
verses.en_bbe: So, then, King Agrippa, I did not go against the vision from heaven;

verses.en: But shewed first unto them of Damascus, and at Jerusalem, and throughout all the coasts of Judaea, and then to the Gentiles, that they should repent and turn to God, and do works meet for repentance.
verses.pt: Mas sim, primeiramente aos que estavam em Damasco e Jerusalém, e por toda a terra da Judeia, e aos gentios anunciei que se arrependessem, e se convertessem a Deus, fazendo obras dignas de arrependimento.
verses.en_web: but declared first to them of Damascus, at Jerusalem, and throughout all the country of Judea, and also to the Gentiles, that they should repent and turn to God, doing works worthy of repentance.
verses.en_bbe: But I went about, first to those in Damascus and Jerusalem, and through all the country of Judaea, and then to the Gentiles, preaching a change of heart, so that they, being turned to God, might give, in their works, the fruits of a changed heart.

verses.en: For these causes the Jews caught me in the temple, and went about to kill me.
verses.pt: Por causa disto os judeus me pegaram no Templo, e procuravam me matar.
verses.en_web: For this reason the Jews seized me in the temple, and tried to kill me.
verses.en_bbe: For this reason, the Jews took me in the Temple, and made an attempt to put me to death.

verses.en: Having therefore obtained help of God, I continue unto this day, witnessing both to small and great, saying none other things than those which the prophets and Moses did say should come:
verses.pt: Porém tendo eu obtido socorro de Deus, permaneço até o dia de hoje, dando testemunho tanto a pequenos como a grandes; não dizendo nada além dos que as coisas que os profetas e Moisés tinham dito que estavam para acontecer;
verses.en_web: Having therefore obtained the help that is from God, I stand to this day testifying both to small and great, saying nothing but what the prophets and Moses said would happen,
verses.en_bbe: And so, by God's help, I am here today, witnessing to small and great, saying nothing but what the prophets and Moses said would come about;

verses.en: That Christ should suffer, and that he should be the first that should rise from the dead, and should shew light unto the people, and to the Gentiles.
verses.pt: Isto é, que o Cristo sofreria, e sendo o primeiro da ressurreição dos mortos, ia anunciar a luz a este povo e aos gentios.
verses.en_web: how the Christ must suffer, and how, by the resurrection of the dead, he would be first to proclaim light both to these people and to the Gentiles.”
verses.en_bbe: That the Christ would go through pain, and being the first to come back from the dead, would give light to the people and to the Gentiles.

verses.en: And as he thus spake for himself, Festus said with a loud voice, Paul, thou art beside thyself; much learning doth make thee mad.
verses.pt: E tendo Paulo dito isto em sua defesa, Festo disse em alta voz: Tu estás louco, Paulo; as muitas escrituras te fizeram enlouquecer!
verses.en_web: As he thus made his defense, Festus said with a loud voice, “Paul, you are crazy! Your great learning is driving you insane!”
verses.en_bbe: And when he made his answer in these words, Festus said in a loud voice, Paul, you are off your head; your great learning has made you unbalanced.

verses.en: But he said, I am not mad, most noble Festus; but speak forth the words of truth and soberness.
verses.pt: Mas ele respondeu: Eu não estou louco, excelentíssimo Festo; mas eu declaro palavras de verdade e de um são juízo;
verses.en_web: But he said, “I am not crazy, most excellent Festus, but boldly declare words of truth and reasonableness.
verses.en_bbe: Then Paul said, I am not off my head, most noble Festus, but my words are true and wise.

verses.en: For the king knoweth of these things, before whom also I speak freely: for I am persuaded that none of these things are hidden from him; for this thing was not done in a corner.
verses.pt: Porque o rei, a quem eu estou falando livremente, ele sabe muito bem destas coisas; porque eu não creio que nenhuma disto lhe seja oculto; por que isto não foi feito num canto.
verses.en_web: For the king knows of these things, to whom also I speak freely. For I am persuaded that none of these things is hidden from him, for this has not been done in a corner.
verses.en_bbe: For the king has knowledge of these things, to whom I am talking freely; being certain that all this is common knowledge to him; for it has not been done in secret.

verses.en: King Agrippa, believest thou the prophets? I know that thou believest.
verses.pt: Rei Agripa, tu crês nos profetas? Eu sei que tu crês.
verses.en_web: King Agrippa, do you believe the prophets? I know that you believe.”
verses.en_bbe: King Agrippa, have you faith in the prophets? I am certain that you have.

verses.en: Then Agrippa said unto Paul, Almost thou persuadest me to be a Christian.
verses.pt: E Agripa disse a Paulo: Por pouco tu me convences a me tornar cristão.
verses.en_web: Agrippa said to Paul, “With a little persuasion are you trying to make me a Christian?”
verses.en_bbe: And Agrippa said to Paul, A little more and you will be making me a Christian.

verses.en: And Paul said, I would to God, that not only thou, but also all that hear me this day, were both almost, and altogether such as I am, except these bonds.
verses.pt: E Paulo disse: Meu desejo a Deus é que, por pouco ou por muito, não somente tu, mas todos os que estão me ouvindo hoje, tais vos tornásseis assim como eu sou, a não ser por estas correntes.
verses.en_web: Paul said, “I pray to God, that whether with little or with much, not only you, but also all that hear me today, might become such as I am, except for these bonds.”
verses.en_bbe: And Paul said, It is my prayer to God that, in little or great measure, not only you, but all those hearing me today might be even as I am, but for these chains.

verses.en: And when he had thus spoken, the king rose up, and the governor, and Bernice, and they that sat with them:
verses.pt: E tendo ele dito isto, o rei se levantou, e também o governador, Berenice, e os que estavam sentados com eles.
verses.en_web: The king rose up with the governor, and Bernice, and those who sat with them.
verses.en_bbe: And the king and the ruler and Bernice and those who were seated with them got up;

verses.en: And when they were gone aside, they talked between themselves, saying, This man doeth nothing worthy of death or of bonds.
verses.pt: E reunindo-se à parte, falavam uns aos outros, dizendo: Este homem nada faz que seja digno de morte ou de prisões.
verses.en_web: When they had withdrawn, they spoke to one another, saying, “This man does nothing worthy of death or of bonds.”
verses.en_bbe: And when they had gone away they said to one another, This man has done nothing which might give cause for death or prison.

verses.en: Then said Agrippa unto Festus, This man might have been set at liberty, if he had not appealed unto Caesar.
verses.pt: E Agripa disse a Festo: Este homem podia ser solto, se ele não tivesse apelado a César.
verses.en_web: Agrippa said to Festus, “This man might have been set free if he had not appealed to Caesar.”
verses.en_bbe: And Agrippa said to Festus, This man might have been made free, if he had not put his cause before Caesar.
